title: Websites and web apps for property managers
meta_description: Websites, listings pages, owner inquiry forms, and portals for property management companies. Fixed price, quoted after a scoping call.
h1: Website and web application development for property management companies
intro: A property management company's website usually has two audiences: prospective tenants looking for available units and an application, and property owners deciding whether to hand over a rental. Many companies run on an AppFolio or Buildium tenant portal for payments and maintenance requests, with a separate marketing site that lists vacancies by hand and links out to the portal. Owner inquiries often arrive through a generic contact form, while rental applications, showing requests, and maintenance forms live in different places.

Creosote Labs builds the marketing site and the tools around it: a listings page that pulls available units from the management platform, an owner inquiry form that collects the property details a manager needs before the first call, and a showing request or maintenance form that lands where staff will see it. Hosting, domain configuration, and documentation are part of the handover. Website and application projects are quoted after a scoping call, at a fixed price with no hourly billing.
projects: A marketing site with services, management fees, and a page for each property type the company handles.
An available-units page that syncs vacancies, photos, and rents from AppFolio or Buildium instead of being updated by hand.
An owner inquiry form that asks for address, unit count, current rent, and condition, and produces a management proposal draft.
A self-scheduling tool for showings that checks the leasing agent's calendar and confirms by text.
A maintenance request form for properties not on the tenant portal that creates a work order and notifies the assigned vendor.
An owner portal for companies whose platform does not include one, with statements, invoices, and inspection reports by property.

faqs.q: We already have a tenant portal through our software. Do we still need a website?
faqs.a: The portal handles payments and requests for existing tenants. A website covers the rest: vacancies, owner acquisition, and the forms that currently go through email or a generic contact page. The two link to each other.

faqs.q: Can the site show our vacancies automatically?
faqs.a: Yes, where the management platform provides a listing feed or API. The scoping call confirms what the platform makes available and the quote reflects it.

faqs.q: How is a website project priced?
faqs.a: Projects are quoted after a scoping call at a fixed price, with no hourly billing. Hosting setup and domain configuration are included in the handover.
